primary_claim: LLMs exhibit feature-specific error correction (FSEC): perturbing residual-stream activations along candidate feature directions (contrastive, MELBO, top-activating SAE latents) produces a stronger downstream response than perturbing along mixtures of those directions, measured as a superellipse exponent p>2 (mean ~2.3 for contrastive, ~2.2 for MELBO/SAE), while non-feature baseline directions (PCA, random, random-difference) give p~2; this replicates across six LLM families and a toy model with ground-truth features (where p=3-3.4), providing the first empirical evidence for computation-in-superposition's predicted error-correction mechanism.

effect.metric: superellipse exponent p for candidate feature directions vs non-feature baselines
effect.value: contrastive directions: mean p=2.42, 95% CI [2.29, 2.62]; MELBO: mean p=2.21, 95% CI [2.01, 2.42]; top-activating SAE latents: mean p=2.28, 95% CI [2.14, 2.47]; PCA baseline: mean p=2.03, 95% CI [1.94, 2.12]; random-difference baseline: mean p=2.05, 95% CI [2.00, 2.10]; random baseline: mean p=2.03, 95% CI [2.00, 2.07]; toy model with ground-truth features: p=3-3.4

stated_future_work: Test whether maximizing the superellipse exponent p directly as an unsupervised feature-finding objective can recover ground-truth features in the toy model
Extend the toy-model validation to standard activation functions and deeper architectures to test how closely a toy model of error correction can reproduce the exponents measured in LLMs
limitations_stated: Preliminary attempts to use p as an unsupervised feature-finding objective (maximizing p directly) did not work: p>2 appears necessary but not sufficient for a direction to be a feature, and maximizing it surfaces high-p directions that don't otherwise behave like features

Activation plateaus, which underlie the measurement, might reflect learned robustness or manifold structure rather than error correction per se, though the core p>2 vs p~2 finding would still hold under this alternative interpretation

The toy model differs significantly from LLMs (two layers, binary features, tanh^3 activation), so its specific p values should not be weighted heavily -- it is intended as methodology validation only
Because ground-truth features are unavailable in LLMs, the measured p (~2.3) is likely a lower bound, since candidate feature directions are only imperfect approximations of the model's true features
quote: We measure $p \approx 2.3$ for contrastive directions and $p \approx 2.2$ for MELBO and SAE directions, against $p \approx 2$ for PCA, random, and random-difference controls.
